+# Index — one line per doc: what it is, what it has authority over, where it stands
+
+A map of `docs/`, not a status board — project state lives on the board and in the workspace.
+Every file under `docs/` appears here exactly once; `archive/`, `evidence/` and `whitepaper/`
+are indexed as wholes. Three conventions carry the map: each doc's own **Status** header is
+authoritative for that doc, `archive/` holds superseded and closed documents, and `reference/`
+holds normative-or-historical sources you consult rather than start from. Triaged 2026-07-28.
+
+## Start here
+
+- `INDEX.md` — this map; the first thing to read in `docs/`, and the redirect of record when a doc moves
+- `omegahive_design_1_1.md` — **the architecture, and the front door.** Our implementation design against the 1.1 spec: assumptions, the write-path invariants R1–R5, the component map, declared divergences, the stage plan (§7) and its gates (§8). Authority: architecture-wide; every other current doc defers to it on structure. Status: current, rev 6 (Jul 6 2026)
+- `omegahive_hive_native_ops.md` — how work actually flows: the hive as its own first workload, the tier ladder, the granularity and steering principles. Authority: tier-1 operations. Status: current, v0.2
+- `omegahive_deployment_spec.md` — repository hygiene, the OmegaClaw fork program, deployment topology and provenance, operating procedures, Beastie bring-up (§7, a completed milestone). Authority: anything you deploy or operate. Status: current, v2 (Jul 7 2026)
+
+## Current — the rest of the operating set
+
+- `omegahive_test_plan.md` — the metrics catalog, suite definitions and decision rules; what "S1 substrate / S2 agents / S3 hive" each mean. Authority: normative for every gate and experiment (the design doc's §8 only summarizes it). Status: current, rev 6 (Jul 6 2026)
+- `omegahive_session_agents.md` — why and how Claude Code / Codex CLI sessions participate as hive workers: wake patterns, the instrumentation ladder, the participation contract. Authority: rationale only — the workspace `WORKER.md` is the operating protocol. Status: current, v1 (Jul 10 2026)
+- `omegahive_ui_spec.md` — the operator-facing web UI: screens, the read-through-the-port architecture, the designed-but-unbuilt write path (§4). Authority: the UI's shape and its hard "must never do" list (§7). Status: current — v0.1 is shipped and serving; the write path is not
+- `omegahive_recovery_runbook.md` — stop/start, backup, restore, drain-before-migrate, environment change. Authority: the operator procedure for a live deployment. Status: current
+- `omegahive_hive_user_migration.md` — moving the stack onto a dedicated `hive` unix account: prep (Parts A–C), cutover (Part D), follow-ups. Status: current, **partially executed** — A–C ran live on Beastie, Part D is deliberately unexecuted and OS separation is still an open Phase 2 gate item

Authority: normative for `qual/` and for any re-qualification run. Status: current, v1.1 — but read `reference/omegahive_stage2_verdict.md` first: the stage-2 pick this fed is closed, and what survives is qualification, not ranking
+
+## Deployment records — `deployments/`
+
+- `deployments/deployment-0-beastie.md` — deployment #0: host facts, lockfile, acceptance and check results. Authority: the record of what Beastie *is*. Status: current, acceptance + checks 1–5 green (Jul 7 2026)
+- `deployments/omegaclaw-fork.md` — the OmegaClaw fork's base and hive images: provenance, lockfiles, the patch set. Authority: the code-provenance record for both images. Status: current, both images built and boot-smoked (Jul 7–8 2026)
+- `deployments/omegahive_remote_access_spec.md` — Tailscale, tailnet-only SSH and web, key-expiry and ACL posture for Beastie. Authority: deployment-#0 practice (a second deployment gets its own record), and the transport the UI spec assumes. Status: current, v1
+
+## Reference — `reference/` (consult; don't start here)
+
+- `reference/README.md` — the two-line convention note for this directory
+- `reference/omegahive_spec_1_1.md` — Ben Goertzel's OmegaHive 1.1 specification, text-faithful conversion of the PDF. Authority: normative for what "1.1 §N" means anywhere in our docs; it is the upstream source, not our plan. Status: reference source (extracted Jul 6 2026; the PDF remains authoritative for formatting)
+- `reference/omegahive_port_spec.md` — the port milestone: the `HiveCoordinatorPort` API, the idempotency key rule, the cursor/read consistency contract, the proof suite. Authority: **binding** — §3's board-validity rule pre-registers any future synthetic coordination test, and §5 is why the default coordinator is mechanical; it describes the past to do it. Status: reference, decided Jul 10 2026
+

+
+Each is self-contained and pinned to a commit or PR; together they are the build record of how

+so they stay on the front path rather than being archived on a guess.

+- `omegahive_v3_kb_persona_brief.md` — authoring brief for the coordinator-v2 persona, the op-reference sheet, and the coordination KB, written blind to board parameters. Status: executed — the artifacts are in `qual/`
+- `omegahive_c2_v0a_v2_order.md` — work order for the v0a v2 battery experiment (the r1 validity review's F1–F6 dispositions turned into a run). Status: **open** — no `qual/records/*-v0a-r2` exists
+- `omegahive_v0b_order.md` — work order for the v0b hive-image board-binding qualification gate; explicitly not a model comparison. Status: **open**, and gated on the v0a-v2 order above
+
+## Directories indexed as wholes
+
+- `archive/` — superseded and closed documents, retained for history and never updated in substance: the pre-1.1 architecture, plan and overview stub, the M0–M5 and v0 build specs, the RP3 shelved draft, the repo-hygiene spec, the Jun-2026 docs audit, the decided OmegaClaw-binding deliberation, and the closed stage-2 spec. Authority: none over current work — each says in its own **Status** header what superseded it. One live residue is flagged there: the stage-2 spec's §7 frozen run config is still the single cited source for the two open qualification orders. See `archive/README.md`
+- `evidence/` — frozen experiment records and analyses: the baseline experiment, the C2 v0a-r1 validity review, the ResearchClawBench triage (spec, report, CSV) and its deep-dive, the competitive and cascade evaluations, the interop/durability notes, the deferred-capability coordination note. Authority: each is the authoritative reading of the run it reports, and none is a plan. Status: frozen — cite them, don't reorganize or edit them
+- `whitepaper/` — LaTeX source and the built PDF for *OmegaHive: A Running Hive*, plus its own build README. Authority: an outward-facing narrative, never a spec; every number in it is meant to be re-derivable from the spine at build date. Status: current artifact, rebuilt on release

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Documentation hygiene checks — link integrity and INDEX completeness.
+
+Two hard checks, no dependencies, no network, no database:
+
+1. **References resolve.** Two classes, everywhere in the tracked tree:
+   every **markdown link** in a `.md` file, and every **`docs/…` path** written
+   in prose or backticks in any text file (README, scripts, module docstrings).
+   Both must point at a file that exists. Fenced code blocks are skipped — they
+   carry code, not references. This is the guard against the silent breakage a
+   docs move causes: `git mv` moves the file, not the sentences pointing at it.
+   Deliberately *not* checked: shorthand module names (`board/legality.py`),
+   container paths, test fixtures, and paths into other repos — none of those
+   are documentation references, and enforcing them buys noise, not integrity.
+
+2. **`docs/INDEX.md` is complete and non-duplicating.** Every file under `docs/`
+   is named exactly once by an index entry — a bullet opening with its path in
+   backticks, relative to `docs/` — or by a directory entry covering it
+   (`archive/`, `evidence/`, `whitepaper/` are indexed as wholes). A doc nobody
+   indexed is a doc nobody can find; a doc indexed twice is two claims about its
+   status. Prose elsewhere in the index may name any path it likes; only entry
+   lines count.
+
+A third, advisory pass reports bare doc *names* mentioned without a path
+(`omegahive_port_spec.md` in prose). Those cannot dangle, but they no longer say
+where the file lives — the index is the redirect. Advisory never fails the run.
+
+    python3 scripts/check_docs.py [--advisory]
+
+Exit status is 0 only if both hard checks pass.
+"""
+

+
+import os
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+INDEX = "docs/INDEX.md"
+# Directories under docs/ that the index covers with one line, as wholes.
+WHOLE_DIRS = ("docs/archive/", "docs/evidence/", "docs/whitepaper/")
+
+TEXT_SUFFIXES = (".md", ".py", ".sh", ".yaml", ".yml", ".toml", ".sql", ".txt", ".tex")
+MD_LINK = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)\s]+)\)")
+# A repo-rooted path into the documentation set, in prose or backticks anywhere.
+# `(?!@)` drops pinned `path@sha` refs: those name a path at a commit, not at HEAD.
+DOCS_PATH = re.compile(r"(?<![\w/])docs/[\w./-]+\.(?:md|csv|tex|pdf|txt)(?!@)")
+DOC_NAME = re.compile(r"\b(omegahive_[\w.-]+\.md)\b")
+FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(```|~~~)")

+INDEX_ENTRY = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s+`([^`]+)`")
+

+    # -z: NUL-separated, so a path with a space or a quote survives intact.
+    out = subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "ls-files", "-z"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
+    )
+    return [p for p in out.stdout.split("\0") if p]

+    """Yield (lineno, text) for lines outside fenced code blocks."""
+    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, path), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:

+        for n, line in enumerate(fh, 1):
+            if FENCE.match(line):
+                in_fence = not in_fence
+                continue
+            if not in_fence:
+                yield n, line.rstrip("\n")

+            targets = []
+            if f.endswith(".md"):
+                targets += [(m.group(1), "link") for m in MD_LINK.finditer(line)]
+            targets += [(m.group(0), "docs-path") for m in DOCS_PATH.finditer(line)]
+            for raw, kind in targets:
+                if raw.startswith(("http://", "https://", "mailto:", "#")):
+                    continue
+                target = raw.split("#")[0]
+                if not target or "://" in target:
+                    continue
+                # A link resolves beside its own file; a docs/ path from the root.
+                base = ROOT if kind == "docs-path" else os.path.join(ROOT, here)
+                checked += 1
+                if not os.path.exists(os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, target))):
+                    failures.append(f"{f}:{n}: dangling {kind} -> {raw}")
+    print(f"references: {checked} checked, {len(failures)} dangling")
+    return failures
+
+
+def check_index(files: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    failures = []
+    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, INDEX)):
+        return [f"{INDEX}: missing"]
+    entries: list[str] = []
+    for _, line in prose_lines(INDEX):
+        m = INDEX_ENTRY.match(line)
+        if m:
+            entries.append(m.group(1))
+    for entry in entries:
+        if entries.count(entry) > 1:
+            failures.append(f"{INDEX}: `{entry}` is entered {entries.count(entry)}x")
+    seen = set(entries)
+    docs = [f for f in files if f.startswith("docs/")]
+    for doc in sorted(docs):
+        rel = doc[len("docs/") :]
+        whole = next((d for d in WHOLE_DIRS if doc.startswith(d)), None)
+        key = whole[len("docs/") :] if whole else rel
+        if key not in seen:
+            what = "no entry covering it" if whole else f"no `{rel}` entry"
+            failures.append(f"{doc}: {what} in {INDEX}")
+        if not whole and rel in seen and any(
+            e.startswith(rel.split("/")[0] + "/") and e.endswith("/") for e in seen
+        ):
+            failures.append(f"{doc}: indexed both as a file and inside a directory entry")
+    stray = [e for e in seen if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", e))]
+    for e in sorted(stray):
+        failures.append(f"{INDEX}: entry `{e}` names nothing under docs/")
+    print(
+        f"index: {len(docs)} files under docs/, {len(set(entries))} entries, "
+        f"{len(failures)} problems"
+    )
+    return sorted(set(failures))
+
+
+def advisory(files: list[str]) -> None:
+    print("\nadvisory — doc names mentioned without a path (the index is the redirect):")
+    for f in files:
+        if not f.endswith(TEXT_SUFFIXES):
+            continue
+        for n, line in prose_lines(f):
+            stripped = DOCS_PATH.sub("", MD_LINK.sub("", line))
+            for m in DOC_NAME.finditer(stripped):
+                print(f"  {f}:{n}: {m.group(1)}")
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    files = tracked_files()
+    failures = check_links(files) + check_index(files)
+    if "--advisory" in sys.argv:
+        advisory(files)
+    if failures:
+        print("\nFAIL")
+        for line in failures:
+            print(f"  {line}")
+        return 1
+    print("\nOK")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+## Reflection
+
+**The order's own numbers were the most useful input and the least reliable one.** "~14 top-level
+`omegahive_*.md` files" is what the survey saw; the directory holds 22. The eight it missed are a
+coherent class — self-contained work orders and post-audit fix lists — which is probably why they
+fell out of a survey framed around "three eras" of specs. They are exactly the docs an outsider
+most misreads, because a file called `omegahive_v0b_order.md` looks identical whether it shipped

+the code) is in; the disposition question is left open rather than answered by a worker who did
